question.:question/problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=-2-(-1)xy?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(1,-1)$,$(2,-2)$,$(-1,-1)$.

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(1,-1)}=-2-(-1)(1)(-1)=-3, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(2,-2)}=-2-(-1)(2)(-2)=-6, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,-1)}=-2-(-1)(-1)(-1)=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting up our points and drawing our line segments, we get the following diagram.

question.:question/problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{(-2)x+(2)y}{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(1,2)$,$(-1,-3)$,$(1,-1)$.

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(1,2)}=\frac{(-2)(1)+(2)(2)}{3}=\frac{2}{3}, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,-3)}=\frac{(-2)(-1)+(2)(-3)}{3}=- \frac{4}{3}, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(1,-1)}=\frac{(-2)(1)+(2)(-1)}{3}=- \frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting up our points and drawing our line segments, we get the following diagram.
